title: Small multiples instead of spaghetti

steps.say: Back to the thirteen coloured lines. Highlighting one region was one way out. Here is the other: give every region a small chart of its own.
facet_wrap() draws one panel per region, all on the same scales, so any two panels can be compared at a glance. The colours and the legend have nothing left to do.
Give every panel the same yardstick. kingdom has no region column, so facet_wrap() cannot split it, and the Kingdom's line is drawn in all thirteen panels.
Order the panels by the change, not by the alphabet, and colour each line by the rule change > 0. The region that went the other way comes first, and it is the only green one.
Short year labels, a title that states the pattern, a subtitle that says what the grey line is. R picks the region for the title with the same rule, change > 0, that coloured its line.

final:
---
title: "Every region, side by side"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
execute:
  echo: false
---

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
all <- read_csv("unemployment.csv")
rates <- all |>
  filter(region != "Kingdom") |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(change = last(rate) - first(rate)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(region = fct_reorder(region, change,
                              .desc = TRUE))
riser <- rates |>
  filter(change > 0) |>
  distinct(region) |>
  pull(region)
kingdom <- all |>
  filter(region == "Kingdom") |>
  select(-region)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5.5
ggplot(rates, aes(date, rate)) +
  geom_line(data = kingdom, colour = "grey70") +
  geom_line(aes(colour = change > 0), linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(vars(region), ncol = 5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#00803A",
                                 `FALSE` = "#4137A8"),
                      guide = "none") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year",
               date_labels = "'%y") +
  labs(title = str_glue(
         "Against the Kingdom, only {riser} ",
         "moved the other way"),
       subtitle = str_glue(
         "Unemployment rate, %. Grey: the Kingdom. ",
         "Ordered by the change since ",
         "{min(rates$quarter)}"),
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```
